title: GIS Ad Hoc Analyses
text:
A working index of small, one-off GIS analyses for WFRC. Each analysis lives in its own folder under projects/, with its own data sources, script/notebook, and outputs. See README.md and CLAUDE.md at the repo root for conventions.
To start a new analysis, copy projects/_template/ (its underscore prefix keeps it – and any other in-progress scaffold folder – out of this published site by convention).

title: Center Buildout Capacity
text:
Estimate additional housing units and jobs at full buildout for three WCV centers:

Daybreak and Saratoga Springs Downtown: from REMM-forecast post-2025 development, applying each center’s median dwelling-unit-per-acre and employment-density (FAR + job-space) assumptions to the forecast residential / commercial-employment development mix.
The Point: from the development schedule the Point team has provided directly, rather than from REMM.

Spatial joins, filtering, and aggregation below run in geopandas/pandas. The base-year parcels come from remm_base_year_data.gdb, which is cached as GeoParquet on first run (see below) so later runs just read that instead of re-parsing the FileGDB.

title: Center Buildout Capacity
section: Daybreak & Saratoga Springs: REMM developable land
text:
Daybreak & Saratoga Springs: REMM developable land
Follows the original pseudocode directly: filter the 2055 buildings table (run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl, one row per building) to parcels within our two centers, keep buildings with year_built > 2025, take the unique parcel ids from that, then sum parcel_acres for those parcels.
An earlier version of this shortcut off the parcel-level parcel_progression_metrics table instead, since it already carries a single year_built per parcel. That’s only valid if every building on a parcel always shares the same year/type – checked directly: 162 parcels regionwide have more than one building, 2 of them are in our two centers, and in both cases the buildings on that parcel happened to share the same year_built. That was a coincidence of this dataset, not something the data guarantees in general, so this now filters at the building level as originally specified rather than relying on it holding elsewhere.


Show the code
buildings_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"],
    columns=["parcel_id", "year_built", "general_type", "residential_units", "job_spaces"],
)

our_parcels = parcels_in_centers[parcels_in_centers["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST)]
buildings_in_centers = buildings_2055.merge(
    our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id"
)

post_2025_parcel_ids = buildings_in_centers.loc[
    buildings_in_centers["year_built"] > 2025, "parcel_id"
].unique()

developable_land = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids)]
    .groupby("CenterName")
    .agg(n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), total_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum"))
    .reset_index()
)

Forecast development mix and buildout capacity
Daybreak and Saratoga Springs Downtown only – The Point’s buildout comes from its own development schedule, not this REMM-based estimate.


Show the code
task2_parcel_ids = our_parcels.loc[
    our_parcels["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2])
    & our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids),
    "parcel_id",
]


Step 1 – residential : jobs ratio. Sum residential_units and job_spaces from parcel_progression_metrics for the same post-2025 developable parcels identified above. These two fields were checked directly against the buildings table and are reliable per-parcel sums across all of a parcel’s buildings (unlike year_built, which only reflects one representative building) – see note above.


Show the code
progression_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["progression_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "residential_units", "job_spaces"]
)

dev_mix = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(task2_parcel_ids)][["parcel_id", "CenterName"]]
    .merge(progression_2055, on="parcel_id")
    .groupby("CenterName")[["residential_units", "job_spaces"]]
    .sum()
)
dev_mix["res_share"] = dev_mix["residential_units"] / (dev_mix["residential_units"] + dev_mix["job_spaces"])
dev_mix["nonres_share"] = 1 - dev_mix["res_share"]

Step 2 – allocate each center’s developable acreage by that ratio.


Show the code
acreage_allocation = developable_land.set_index("CenterName").loc[
    CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2], ["total_acres"]
].join(dev_mix[["res_share", "nonres_share"]])
acreage_allocation["res_acres"] = acreage_allocation["total_acres"] * acreage_allocation["res_share"]
acreage_allocation["nonres_acres"] = acreage_allocation["total_acres"] * acreage_allocation["nonres_share"]

Step 3 – median capacity assumptions. Per Josh’s guidance, “median” means the midpoint of the standard planning range for the center’s type (all three of ours are “Urban Center”: FAR 0.75-4.0, DUA 20-100) – not a statistical median computed from the parcels table’s own max_far/max_dua columns. The DwellingPerAcre/NonResFAR fields on the REST-cached center layer already carry each center’s own range string, so this parses those directly.


Show the code
def range_midpoint(range_str):
    lo, hi = range_str.split("-")
    return (float(lo) + float(hi)) / 2


capacities = centers_preview.set_index("CenterName").loc[
    CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2], ["DwellingPerAcre", "NonResFAR"]
]
capacities["median_dua"] = capacities["DwellingPerAcre"].apply(range_midpoint)
capacities["median_far"] = capacities["NonResFAR"].apply(range_midpoint)

Step 4 – sqft-per-job assumption, from each center’s own post-2025 non-residential buildings. sqft_per_job turns out to be a fixed constant per building general_type region-wide (Office 633, Retail 374, Industrial 975, …), so taking the median here reflects each center’s forecast non-res building mix rather than sampling noise.


Show the code
buildings_full = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "year_built", "general_type", "sqft_per_job"]
).merge(our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id")

nonres_post_2025 = buildings_full[
    (buildings_full["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2]))
    & (buildings_full["year_built"] > 2025)
    & ~buildings_full["general_type"].isin(["SF Residential", "MF Residential"])
]
sqft_per_job = nonres_post_2025.groupby("CenterName")["sqft_per_job"].median().rename("sqft_per_job")

Step 5 – combine into full-buildout capacity.


Show the code
SQFT_PER_ACRE = 43_560

capacity = acreage_allocation.join(capacities[["median_dua", "median_far"]]).join(sqft_per_job)
capacity["housing_units"] = capacity["res_acres"] * capacity["median_dua"]
capacity["nonres_sqft"] = capacity["nonres_acres"] * capacity["median_far"] * SQFT_PER_ACRE
capacity["jobs"] = capacity["nonres_sqft"] / capacity["sqft_per_job"]

title: Center Buildout Capacity
text:
REMM parcels: DuckDB spatial setup


Show the code
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw"),
    "processed": Path("_data/processed"),
}
paths["processed"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

paths.update({
    "gdb": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "remm_base_year_data.gdb",
    "progression_2023_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2023_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "progression_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2055_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "parcels_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "parcels_2023.parquet",
    "centers_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "centers.parquet",
    "progression_2023_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2023.parquet",
    "progression_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2055.parquet",
})

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("INSTALL spatial")
con.execute("LOAD spatial")

# one-time geopandas/pyogrio read of the two vector sources DuckDB can't parse
# itself (the gdb) or that we'd otherwise re-fetch every run (the gpkg), cached
# as GeoParquet -- geopandas.to_parquet() writes correct CRS metadata natively.
if not paths["parcels_geoparquet"].exists():
    parcels_gdf = gpd.read_file(paths["gdb"], layer="parcels", columns=["parcel_id", "parcel_acres"])
    parcels_gdf.to_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])

if not paths["centers_geoparquet"].exists():
    centers_gdf = gpd.read_file(L["center_boundaries"], columns=["CenterName", "CenterType"])
    centers_gdf.to_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"])

con.execute(f"""
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW parcels AS
    SELECT parcel_id, parcel_acres, geometry AS geom
    FROM read_parquet('{paths["parcels_geoparquet"].as_posix()}')
""")
con.execute(f"""
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW centers AS
    SELECT CenterName, CenterType, ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:26912', true) AS geom
    FROM read_parquet('{paths["centers_geoparquet"].as_posix()}')
""")


<_duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection at 0x24cc7727b30>




Show the code
# only the parcel-level progression metrics tables for now -- they already carry
# year_built, was_developed/was_redeveloped, developable, and acreage_dev/redev
# (split res vs. nonres) per parcel, so the building-level tables aren't needed
# for this step. Converted once to parquet so DuckDB doesn't round-trip pandas.
for key in ["progression_2023", "progression_2055"]:
    dst = paths[f"{key}_parquet"]
    if not dst.exists():
        pd.read_pickle(paths[f"{key}_pkl"]).to_parquet(dst)
    con.execute(f"CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {key} AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{dst.as_posix()}')")

title: Center Buildout Capacity
section: REMM parcels: load and cache as parquet
text:
REMM parcels: load and cache as parquet


Show the code
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw"),
    "processed": Path("_data/processed"),
}
paths["processed"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

paths.update({
    "gdb": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "remm_base_year_data.gdb",
    "buildings_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl",
    "progression_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2055_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "parcels_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "parcels_2023.parquet",
    "centers_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "centers.parquet",
    "buildings_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "buildings_2055.parquet",
    "progression_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2055.parquet",
})

# one-time read of the two vector sources, cached as GeoParquet so later runs
# don't re-parse the FileGDB or re-fetch the REST layer.
if not paths["parcels_geoparquet"].exists():
    parcels_gdf = gpd.read_file(paths["gdb"], layer="parcels", columns=["parcel_id", "parcel_acres"])
    parcels_gdf.to_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])

if not paths["centers_geoparquet"].exists():
    centers_gdf = gpd.read_file(
        L["center_boundaries"],
        columns=["CenterName", "CenterType"],
        where=f"CenterName IN ({', '.join(map(repr, CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))}) AND CenterType = 'Urban Center'",
    )
    centers_gdf.to_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"])

if not paths["buildings_2055_parquet"].exists():
    buildings_full = pd.read_pickle(paths["buildings_2055_pkl"]).reset_index()
    # 'note' mixes strings with an int 0 sentinel (no dedicated null), which pyarrow
    # can't write as a single column type -- cast to string so every row survives
    # as-is (0 -> "0") rather than dropping columns to sidestep the type error.
    buildings_full["note"] = buildings_full["note"].astype(str)
    buildings_full.to_parquet(paths["buildings_2055_parquet"])

if not paths["progression_2055_parquet"].exists():
    pd.read_pickle(paths["progression_2055_pkl"]).to_parquet(paths["progression_2055_parquet"])

parcels = gpd.read_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])
centers = gpd.read_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"]).to_crs(parcels.crs)

title: Center Buildout Capacity
text:
Centers of interest
Single ordered list to extend if more centers are added later. center_boundaries is fetched in full from the REST service (no server-side where), so adding a center here doesn’t require touching sources.yml or re-fetching – just delete _data/processed/centers.parquet to force it to rebuild with the updated list. Subsets below are index slices into this same list: [0:2] for the two REMM-method centers (Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown), [2:3] for The Point.
Every gpd.read_file() call below passes an OGR SQL where built straight from that list, restricted to “Urban Center” polygons (drops The Point’s separate “Employment District” polygon, since every center in scope for this analysis is its Urban Center polygon).


Show the code
CENTERS_OF_INTEREST = ["Daybreak", "Saratoga Springs Downtown", "The Point"]
